headline: The real house, rebuilt room by room until a critic stops telling them apart
lede: Every room of this house is being rebuilt as procedural 3D geometry inside the live Home Assistant app, then screenshotted from the same spot the reference photo was taken. A separate critic with fresh context puts the two side by side, blind, and says which is which. If ours is obvious, it goes back to the builder. The bar for the overall look is The Sims 4's dollhouse build view; the bar for each room is the photograph of that actual room.
stamp: round 2 built on 3 rooms · paused at the API session limit
hero_label: First floor as it stands: Dining with its real bay, Kitchen, and Living Room with the fireplace on the chimney chase — daylight coming through openings that are actually cut. The garage and hallway are still the bare shells everything started as.

rooms.name: Master Bedroom
rooms.note: Three rounds of careful measurement — the bed was proved a queen, not a king, by three photo anchors, and the vault ridge was measured to sit over the bed. The re-trace then rotated the room's long axis 90 degrees, so every wall assignment has to be re-derived. The measurement work carries over; the placement does not.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.note: Round 2: the fake internal wall and its 190 sq ft of dead floor are gone with the re-trace, the fridge run stands against the real wall, and real cut openings mean you now look over the peninsula half-wall at the living room fireplace the way photos C and F do. Floor rebuilt as 7.4 in planks in six greys (tonal spread 24-51 against the photo's 27.3, where round 1 was 9.5), contact shadows baked under everything, black knobs on doors. Wall-value spread within the room 93 -> 56 bytes with no emissive wash.

rooms.name: Living Room
rooms.note: Round 2 made a structural correction: the floor plan draws the north-west chamfer as a thickened wall — a chimney chase — and two photos show the stone breast on a wall angled to the TV wall. The fireplace belongs there, not on the north wall, which freed that wall to hold exactly what the plan draws. Stone rebuilt as a jittered Voronoi tessellation rather than courses of rectangles. Pickability recovered from 33% to 61% by naming the rug as a surface.

rooms.name: Dining
rooms.note: Round 1 built. Footprint since re-traced to 14.6 x 13.1 with a real canted east bay — which solves round 1's stated limitation that the geometry could not hold the bay. Needs re-placing into it.

rooms.name: Rios Room
rooms.note: Critic FAILED round 1: windows built 6.15 ft tall against ~4.8 measured, so they read as French doors and made the room look oversized. The re-trace then shrank the room from 15.5 x 16 to 12.5 x 11.7 — vindicating the critic. Needs re-placing plus the 12-item list.
